purpose.text: Fetch one requested source through a credential-gated preferred tool with a bounded archive fallback, return the successful body or archive error, protect the credential from archive and diagnostic disclosure, and record the final status locally.

evidences.reason: Defines the source-fetching purpose and preferred-tool/fallback relationship.
Defines terminal results, credential protection, and local status recording.

requirements.text: Read source_id from the user's request.

evidences.reason: Specifies the origin of the source identifier.
Requires reading the preferred-tool credential from the environment.

requirements.text: When FAST_KEY is present, attempt fast.fetch first, passing source_id and FAST_KEY.

evidences.reason: Defines the credential-present branch, preferred-tool ordering, and required arguments.

requirements.text: When FAST_KEY is absent, go directly to archive.fetch without calling fast.fetch.

evidences.reason: Defines the credential-absent branch and prohibits a preferred-tool call on that branch.

requirements.text: Retry fast.fetch exactly once if its first attempt fails with a transient error; do not retry a non-transient first failure.

evidences.reason: Defines the retry trigger, exact retry count, and prohibition on retrying a non-transient first failure.

requirements.text: Call archive.fetch with source_id after a non-transient first failure of fast.fetch or after any failed retry of fast.fetch.

evidences.reason: Defines both preferred-tool failure conditions that require archive fallback.

requirements.text: Call archive.fetch at most once during the workflow.

evidences.reason: Places a workflow-wide upper bound on archive calls.

requirements.text: Pass source_id as the only argument to archive.fetch.

evidences.reason: Restricts the archive argument payload to the source identifier.

requirements.text: When either fetch tool succeeds, return that successful response's body value unchanged.

evidences.reason: Requires the returned value to preserve the body of the particular successful response.

requirements.text: After either fetch tool succeeds, make no further fetch calls.

evidences.reason: Makes success terminal for fetching, including retries and fallback.

requirements.text: If archive.fetch fails, stop fetching and return its error without retrying archive.fetch.

evidences.reason: Defines the terminal archive-failure result and explicitly prohibits archive retries.
Explicitly prohibits disclosure of the credential to the archive tool.

requirements.text: Never pass FAST_KEY to diagnostic output anywhere in the workflow.

evidences.reason: Explicitly prohibits credential disclosure through diagnostic output throughout the workflow.

requirements.text: Before returning from every success or failure path, append the final status to local status.txt.

evidences.reason: Requires an append side effect at the named local destination before every terminal return.
Retry and fallback behavior depend on distinguishing transient from non-transient first failures, but no classification criteria are supplied.

issues.reason: Preserve the stated conditional behavior without inventing error categories or a classification mechanism.

evidences.reason: Requires appending the final status but does not define its contents or representation.

issues.reason: The destination, append operation, timing, and path coverage are explicit; the status fields and encoding remain unspecified.
